sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed by the petitioner challenging order dated 04.02.2022 (Annexure P-7) vide which petitioner was placed under suspension by the Superintendent of Police, Jabalpur.
2.

When the petitioner is asked that whether she had preferred any appeal against the order of suspension, she submits that she has not filed any appeal against the order of suspension, inasmuch as, she has impleaded Superintendent of Police, Jabalpur as a party in his personal capacity,
inasmuch as, the order of suspension is laced with malafides.
3. It is submitted that petitioner was posted in District Ujjain and vide order dated 25.03.2021 was transferred to District Jabalpur.
She had given her joining as Station House Officer, Police Station Gorakhpur on 21.08.2021 after being posted at Police Lines, Jabalpur for a while.
She performed her duties with utmost sincerity and honesty as can be seen from the comparative chart of registration of cases and investigation carried out by her as contained in Annexure P-1.

She was rewarded from time to time but many a times she had a feeling that respondent No.3 was biased towards her,
inasmuch as, vide Annexure P-2 dated 18.01.2022, Letters of Appreciation were issued and directed to be recorded in the service book of the concerned officers, namely, Sub Inspector Shehnarayan Dubey, Sub Inspector Sangeeta Choudhary and Sub Inspector Shehmani Tiwari of Gorakhpur police station but petitioner was left out, when petitioner was compelled to make a communication as contained in Annexure P-3 to the Superintendent of Police pointing out that Police Station Gorakhpur had taken up 53 cases in e-investigation and was the first in the whole district.
She pointed out that Inspectors posted at Police Station Cantonment and Garha which stood second and third respectively, were given appreciation but name of the petitioner was left out.

She pointed out that there was definitely some error in making evaluation of her performance and, therefore,
demanded that she too be bestowed with appreciation and same be recorded in her service book.
4. It is submitted that probably this enraged the Superintendent of Police, resulting in passing of the orders of suspension.

It is submitted that respondent No.3 was not acting bonafidely and though as per the work distribution, CSP Kotwali was authorized to conduct Departmental Enquiries against the Station House Officer, Police Station Gorakhpur but overlooking the work distribution memo,
Superintendent of Police directed his blue eyed boys/girls to conduct the enquiries which were conducted in the manner in which Superintendent of Police desired recording findings against the petitioner causing bias to her and that resulted in her order of suspension.
5.

It is submitted that the petitioner was working under the guidance of the Superintendent of Police and was following his orders as can be seen from the transcript contained in Annexure RJ-34 and the communication contained in Annexure RJ-35.

It is submitted that Annexure RJ-35 is the complaint given by Sandeep Bagde, pointing out the lapses and biased actions of the Enquiry officer,
CSP Bargi, Priyanka Shukla but no cognizance of all these material was taken and she was being maligned unnecessarily.
6.
It is submitted that a case was reported by the local MLA Shri Tarun Bhanot but since that case was within the jurisdiction of Omti Police Station, it was registered at Omti Police Station.

It was neither registered at Gorakhpur police station nor investigated by the Gorakhpur police station but when it came to some public demonstration at Chhoti Line then malafidely newspaper reporting was Archana Nagar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52068115/
2 made that, that demonstration was against the present petitioner.

Pointing out this fact it is submitted that there was a plot to frame the present petitioner as she was gaining popularity due to her hard work and therefore, had become an eye sore for several other persons, who under the leadership of the Superintendent of Police colluded to malign her.

8. Placing reliance on the judgment of Supreme Court in Ajay Kumar Choudhary Vs. Union of India through its Secretary and another, (2015) 7 SCC 291, it is submitted that there is a requirement for periodic review of the order of suspension.

sentences.text: Petitioner is languishing under suspension for over 14 months and no review is taken till date because respondent No.3 is having good connections and is not allowing any legal thing to happen in the matter of the petitioner.

9. Similarly, reliance is placed on the judgment of the Delhi High Court in Kamlapati Dubey Vs.
Union of India, 1998 (2) SLR 137, wherein it is held that if a person is a victim of personal bias and prejudices then consequent orders passed by them needs to be set aside and they are required to be reinstated.
10.

sentences.text: Similarly, reliance is placed on the order of a coordinate Bench decision in Shambhu Prasad Gupta Vs. Managing Director, Madhya Pradesh State Civil Supplies Corporation Ltd., Bhopal and another (W.P. No.12440/2017 decided on 13.09.2017).

sentences.text:
Placing reliance on these judgments it is submitted that petitioner is victim of bias of respondent No.3.
11.

Reliance is also placed on GAD memo No.10163-2116-1 dated 09.12.1958, which provides that a Government servant against whom a departmental enquiry is contemplated, should not be placed under suspension merely as a matter of course.

It is only when the allegation or charges are of a grave and serious nature or when it is necessary so to do on administrative consideration or for other cogent reasons that the Government servant concerned, should be placed under suspension where it is unavoidable.

As an alternative to suspension, the suspending authority concerned,
should consider the advisability of posting the accused official to another station.
In case he is found to be tampering with evidence, his presence is otherwise prejudicial to the enquiry.

Government desire that the Secretariat department concerned should obtain full details in each case from the subordinate authority concerned and ensure that the suspensions are justified and reasonable.
12. It is submitted that the order of suspension is ante dated.

Petitioner was called by the Superintendent of Police on 4th, she was suffering from Blood Pressure fluctuation and not keeping good health, therefore, on 5th morning, certain staff sent by the Superintendent of Police had walked into her bedroom and had seen the condition of the petitioner.

Petitioner was pressurized to withdraw her case as was filed on 04.02.2022, vide which petitioner had challenged order of line attachment but when she refused then Superintendent of Police passed order of suspension in back date on 4th February, 2022, which is indicative of malafide.
13. Shri Bramhadatt Singh, learned Deputy Advocate General, in his turn, submits that in their return they have shown the past conduct of the petitioner.

Since she was inducted as a Archana Nagar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52068115/
3 Sub-Inspector in the Madhya Pradesh police service on 20.05.1999.

sentences.text: It is submitted that she was trapped by the Lokayukt police in a bribery case.
She was convicted then dismissed but on acquittal in CRA No.2325/2006, she was reinstated back in service in view of acquittal.

While she was posted as Sub-Inspector, State Crime Bureau, PHQ, Bhopal, case regarding slapping, abusing and manhandling, a lady Railway employee was registered against the petitioner under Section 323, 294,
IPC.
Thereafter, another case was registered against her at Police Station Govindpura under Section 419, 420, 34 of IPC regarding cheating the informant of Rs.26,23,900/-.
Similarly, other punishments as were inflicted on her are mentioned in the impugned table.

14. Thus, it is submitted that petitioner's past is tardy and keeping in view all these facts, order of suspension was passed, especially, after taking into consideration enquiry reports which were submitted by the concerned CSPs/Additional SPs against the petitioner.
15.

Placing reliance on such reports dated 18.01.2022 submitted by CSP, Gorakhpur, dated 02.02.2022 submitted by Additional SP (City), Jabalpur and dated 03.02.2022, it is submitted that there is plethora of material against the malfunctioning of the petitioner and, therefore, she was placed under suspension.

16. Reliance is also placed on the report dated 04.02.2022 passed by the Additional SP, Town North,
Jabalpur and 04.03.2022 issued by the CSP, Bargi that there is sufficient material on record to take action against the petitioner.
17. It is submitted that after issuance of suspension order, charge- sheet has been issued in time and enquiry is being conducted against the petitioner, which is underway.
18. Shri K.C. Ghildiyal, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent No.3 submits that there are bald allegations against the respondent No.3.
They do not fulfill the requirements to demonstrate either malafide or arbitrariness.
It is submitted that conduct of the petitioner is writ large.

19. Petitioner in person submits that she has explanation for all the past conducts, which have been highlighted by learned Deputy Advocate General in his return filed on behalf of respondents No.1 and 2.
She was acquitted by the High Court.
It was a matter of personal transaction between her father and another person in which police has filed F/R but State has deliberately not brought on record complete facts.
It is submitted that suspension order could not have been influenced by the past conduct.

This admission of the respondents of being influenced by the past conduct is a ground to quash the order of suspension as it is not made with immediate concern or consideration but looking to the past conduct and also taking a fact into consideration that concocted enquiry reports,
which were obtained by the Superintendent of Police, Jabalpur so to malign the character of the present petitioner who was forced to do illegal things and when she showed some resistance then,
Superintendent of Police got her framed.
20.

In support of these contentions, she has referred to the transcripts contained in Annexure RJ-25 and RJ-34, to show that how Superintendent of Police was trying to influence the course of Archana Nagar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52068115/
4 investigation and save certain influential persons and was using abusive language towards the petitioner, which was unbecoming of an officer on the part of the Superintendent of Police-respondent No.3 Shri Siddharth Bahuguna.

sentences.text: 21. After hearing petitioner in person and the learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is true that suspension order notes down certain violations of the Police Regulation.
It is also true that petitioner is languishing under suspension since 04.02.2022.
Ratio of law laid down by Supreme Court in Ajay Kumar Choudhary Vs. Union of India and others (supra) is that there should be periodic review of suspension orders.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: GAD memo dated 09.12.1958 substantiate this.
Long suspension is neither good for the State nor for the health of the affected person.
There are limits to judicial review.

Though petitioner has made allegations of malafide against the respondent No.3 but they could not be substantiated except that enquiries were got conducted through those persons, who were not competent as per the work distribution, inasmuch as, the CSP Kotwali, who was competent and authorized to conduct enquiries in the conduct of the officials of the Gorakhpur police station, was deliberately kept away from the said exercise for which no reason is given by the learned Deputy Advocate General or the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent No.3.
22.

However, reliance is placed on the judgment of the Supreme Court in Indian Railway Construction Company Ltd. Vs. Ajay Kumar, (2003) 4 SCC 579, wherein in para 23, it is held as under:-
''Doubtless, he who seeks to invalidate or nullify any act or order must establish the charge of bad faith, an abuse or a misuse by the authority of its powers.

entities.text: Indian Railway Construction Company Ltd. Vs. Ajay Kumar, (2003) 4 SCC 579
entities.label: PRECEDENT

While the indirect motive or purpose, or bad faith or personal ill will is not to be held established except on clear proof thereof, it is obviously difficult to establish the state of a man's mind, for that is what the employee has to establish in this case, though this may sometimes be done.''
23. Thus in absence of any direct material to show malafide, especially when petitioner was being suitably rewarded from time to time for her good deeds and rebuked for her act of deviation, and there being limits to the judicial review of an order of suspension and it is held in State of Orrisa Vs.
Vimal Kumar Mohanti, (1994) 4 SCC 126, AIR 1994 SC 2296, that normally the Courts will not interfere with orders of suspension, pending enquiry unless good grounds like malafide are made out as held in State of Uttar Pradesh Vs. Vishwanath Prasad (Dr.), 1995 Supp. (2) SC 145.
24.

Taking this fact also into consideration that when the order of suspension if appealable then, the interference by judicial review will not be SAN proper as held by the Supreme Court in S.A. Khan Vs.
State of Haryana, AIR 1993 SC 1152 , this Court is of the view that in view of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Ajay Kumar Chaudhary (supra), petitioner is relegated to avail the remedy of appeal and if she files appeal within 15 days of receipt of certified copy of the order being passed today, then appellate authority is advised to not advert to the issue of limitation and decide her appeal on its own merits, also keeping in view the principles laid down by the Supreme Court for reviewing the suspension order and the guidelines of the GAD that it is not advisable to keep a Government servant under suspension for long durations on its own merits, without getting Archana Nagar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52068115/
